children.text: Mount Talinis is the second-highest peak on Negros after Kanlaon Volcano, and it is also called Cuernos de Negros ("Horns of Negros") for its horn-like summits. The classic trek is a 2-day, 1-night hike past Lake Yagumyum and Lake Nailig, through sulfur vents and mossy forest, and a registered guide is required.

Mount Talinis is a volcanic complex rising in southern Negros Oriental, and it is the second-highest mountain on Negros after Kanlaon. Wikipedia gives its elevation as 1,862 m, while hiking guides and trek reports give about 1,903 m, so the figure differs by source. This guide says
roughly 1,900 m
and suggests you follow local information for the exact number. It lies about
20 km
southwest of Dumaguete and about
9 km

from Valencia town proper, so it is fairly close to the city. The group of summits in this area looks like horns, which gave rise to the nickname Cuernos de Negros ("Horns of Negros"), and Talinis is the highest peak of that range.

Geologically, Talinis is a complex volcano belonging to the Negros volcanic belt. The Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) is reported to classify it as potentially active, and the date of its last eruption is unknown. The rocks are mostly Late Miocene andesite and basalt, and the base of the volcanic complex is about
36 km

across. Besides Talinis itself, the complex includes Magaso, Guinsayawan, Yagumyum Peak and the Guintabon Dome. The slopes have steam vents and sulfur zones, some of which are used for geothermal power, and the Southern Negros geothermal field (Palinpinon) in Valencia is listed as 192.5 MW on Wikipedia, while a 2024 report gives about 221.8 MW across its operating plants, so figures differ by source.

The appeal of this mountain lies less in the summit than in the lakes and forest along the way. The twin crater lakes Balinsasayao and Danao lie inside the Guintabon Caldera, and near the top you find Lake Yagumyum, Lake Nailig and Lake Mabilog in turn. Hikers usually pitch tents beside Lake Nailig and spend the night there. One trek report calls it one of the most scenic and coldest campsites in the Visayas. Both lakes have water you can use to top up your supply, and swimming is said to be possible. The routes fall into two broad groups. The most common is the Apolong route, which starts in Apolong village in Valencia and passes the Kaipuhan sulfur vents and Lake Nailig. The Bediao route starts at the Bediao geothermal area in Dauin and passes Lake Yagumyum and Lake Nailig. A 2009 trek report described a traverse that went up from Bediao and down to Apolong, rating it a major climb of about
10–11 hours

to the summit and about 6 out of 9 in difficulty. The same report named the Cuernos de Negros Mountaineers (CNMCI), based at Silliman University in Dumaguete, as a contact for planning a climb, but that information is old, so check contact details locally. If a trek feels like too much, you can instead make a day of the foothill sights in Valencia, such as Casaroro Falls or Forest Camp.

The mountain is also ecologically valuable. Wikipedia records 91 tree species in the area, 18 of them commercially important, and wild orchids and broad-leafed tree ferns are common. Animals include wild boar, civets, monkeys, sunbirds and monitor lizards, and rare species such as the tarictic hornbill, the Philippine spotted deer, the Visayan warty pig and the Negros bleeding-heart are also said to live here. At the same time, illegal logging, slash-and-burn farming, rising tourism and housing development are cited as threats to its biodiversity. Walking only on the marked trail with a guide and carrying out all your trash is the easiest way to help protect this mountain.

This crater lake below the summit is the center of the trek, where you pitch your tent and enjoy the stars and the mist. The lake is clear and cold, and the view around sunset is lovely. Follow your guide's instructions on where to camp and on the rules.
This is described as an ancient crater lake, and swimming is said to be possible. A side trail of about
30 minutes
up from the lake leads to Yagumyum Peak, which is optional.
A round lake right next to Lake Nailig. Local stories say snakes hide there, so follow your guide's advice near the water.
A sulfur-venting zone you meet midway along the Apolong route. The smell is strong and the ground can be unstable, so do not leave the marked path. A mask is useful.
On the mid-slopes the forest is thick with moss and old trees. Frequent mist gives the forest a mysterious mood.
It takes about
30 minutes
to walk from Lake Nailig to the highest point. This peak is also called Nailig Peak or Talinis Dako. The forest is dense and mist is frequent, so the view is not always open.
One side starts at Bediao in Dauin and the other at Apolong in Valencia. You can go up one side and down the other, and the descent is known to pass the sulfur river and Casaroro Falls.
A forest of wild orchids, tree ferns and constant birdsong. It is a threatened habitat, so do not feed or touch the animals.

items.title: 2-day, 1-night Apolong route
items.subtitle: Climb from Valencia and spend a night at the lake

children.text: Take a jeepney or multicab from Dumaguete to Valencia. The ride takes about
20–30 minutes
, and you can handle registration and permits at the Valencia market or tourism office.
Take a motorcycle taxi from Valencia market to Apolong village. The ride takes about
20–30 minutes
Start the climb with your guide. The forest is thick, so it is relatively cool.
Pass through the sulfur vent zone, wearing a mask and following your guide's instructions.
Pitch your tent beside Lake Nailig and cook dinner. Temperatures drop a lot at night.

Times vary greatly with fitness and weather. Guides usually describe the trek as 2 days and 1 night or 3 days and 2 nights. If it rains the trail gets slippery, so do not push on and follow your guide's judgment.
Set out for the summit before dawn. It is about
30 minutes
from the lake.
Return to camp, eat breakfast and pack up.
Start the descent. On the Bediao traverse, the route is known to pass the sulfur river and Casaroro Falls.
From the Casaroro Falls entrance, take a motorcycle taxi to Valencia town.
Take a jeepney back to Dumaguete.
These descent times are only examples from a trek guide. Leave a margin so that you finish the descent before dark.
There are direct flights from Manila to Dumaguete-Sibulan Airport (DGT). Check flight times and fares on the airline's website for your dates.
From the airport, go into the city by tricycle or taxi. For getting from Dumaguete to Valencia, see the local transport section below.
Ceres buses run from Bacolod South Bus Terminal to Dumaguete via Mabinay and are said to take about
6–7 hours
After arriving in Dumaguete, take a jeepney or multicab to Valencia.

items.title: From Dumaguete to Valencia and Apolong

children.text: Take a jeepney or multicab to Valencia from near the Dumaguete public market or around Rizal Boulevard. It takes about
20–30 minutes
From Valencia market, take a motorcycle taxi to the Apolong village entrance. It takes about
20–30 minutes
The Bediao route starts on the Dauin side. Check transport and fares locally.
Guided group treks sometimes include transport.

The dry season, November to May, is best for walking. Guides consistently advise avoiding the rainy season, when trails are slippery and landslides are possible. Even in the dry season, temperatures are low and mist is frequent high up, so warm clothing is necessary.
For a multi-day trek, check the weather forecast before you leave. Weather on the mountain changes quickly, and even on a clear day it can rain in the afternoon.

There is no lodging on the mountain, so bring a tent or arrange equipment through your guide. Lake Nailig is the most common campsite, and people also camp beside Lake Yagumyum. Valencia and Dumaguete have many hotels and guesthouses, which are good places to stay before and after the climb.
You have to carry all your food up the mountain. Pack cooking gear, food, at least about
3 liters
of water and purification tablets. Water can be refilled at the lakes, but always boil or purify it before drinking. After the descent, enjoy local food at a restaurant in Dumaguete.

It is a good idea to stay in Valencia or Dumaguete the night before and confirm the time with your guide. A trek guide lists the Valencia Tourism Office at mobile 0927 810 4644 and email tourism.valenciagor@gmail.com, but these may change.
A registered guide is required. Register and get your permit at the Valencia Tourism Office.
Many sections are slippery and muddy, so bring shoes with good grip and trekking poles.
Cover your backpack with a waterproof cover and pack warm layers and a rain jacket.
Bring a headlamp with spare batteries, a first-aid kit and any personal medication.
Signal is weak in many places, so download offline maps.
In the sulfur zone, wear a mask and walk only on the path your guide chooses.
Carry out all your trash and do not disturb plants or animals.
If you reach your limit, turning back is always the safest choice.
A day hike is described as possible, but most guides recommend a night at Lake Nailig. If your schedule is tight, shorten the route rather than rush.
You will need a motorcycle taxi on the way down, so carry cash in small bills. There are no ATMs in the mountain villages.
This is volcanic terrain, so watch for sulfur gas and unstable ground, and in the rainy season landslides are a risk, so do not climb without a guide.
Sources disagree on the elevation, giving about 1,862 to 1,903 m. Your app may show a different figure.
Permit and guide fees can change with the season, so confirm them with the tourism office before you go.
One trek report mentions past rumors of New People's Army (NPA) presence. Check the latest local safety advisories before you depart.
Fog and rain on the mountain make it easy to lose body heat. Change out of wet clothes quickly.
Do not hike alone, and tell your lodging your plan and expected return time.
A waterfall of about
or more, met on the descent of the Bediao traverse, described as the highest waterfall on Negros.
Twin crater lakes inside the Talinis volcanic complex, designated a natural park.
The university city with an airport that serves as the starting base for the trek.
A coastal town with the starting point of the Bediao route, known for diving.
